items.title: NEW — `Style::attribute` takes `value: Option<str>`: today it matches an EXACT value only (`[name="value"]`, style.vl:1470), so a PRESENCE condition (`[data-selected]`, `[disabled]`) has no spelling and kolt reaches for the `children`/`divide` chokepoint `child_relation("[data-selected]", ..)` (public only because vilan has no visibility) as a raw-selector escape hatch — and hits its v1 fence the moment a `.hover` nests inside ("takes an unconditioned style"); `None` = presence, `Some(v)` = exact match. The NEGATED form (`:not([disabled])`) is the sibling gap: `pseudo("not([disabled])", hover(..))` is refused as two pseudo-classes in one slot, so 'not disabled AND hovered' is spellable only by carrying the state as an attribute VALUE (`attribute("data-disabled", "false", hover(..))` → `.sX[data-disabled="false"]:hover`, which works today)
items.discussion: the owner's ask (2026-09-11) from kolt's `new_button_style` exploration (styles.vl:52 — the A84 shape: state as data attributes selected by static rules, `--button-color` as the theme var); the error the owner saw in the editor was `child_relation`'s const-time refusal, hidden from `vilan check` by four earlier errors; ui-styling.md §846 records the unconditioned-inner fence as v1
items.body:
**Today.** `attribute(self, name: str, value: str, inner: Style)` (style.vl:1470) renders `[name="value"]` and validates both tokens at const time; `pseudo` (:1502) allows one pseudo-class per slot; `child_relation` (:1432) refuses any conditioned inner because a pseudo under a child combinator would bind to the child's compound. kolt's `new_button_style` (styles.vl:52) wants `.sX[data-selected]{color}` and `.sX:not([disabled]):hover{background}` and can spell neither.

**The change.** (1) `attribute(name, value: Option<str>, inner)`: `Some(v)` renders `[name="v"]` as today, `None` renders `[name]` (presence). In a `css` block the nested-rule head takes ordinary expressions, so `.attribute("data-selected", None) { .. }` reads as written; the slot key stays one attribute per slot. Every existing call site passes `Some(..)` — a mechanical sweep of std, docs and examples (kolt at the owner's word); OR keep the two-argument form and add `attribute_present(name, inner)` beside it if the `Some` noise at every call is judged worse than a second name — say which, the recommendation is the `Option` (one concept, the owner's ask). (2) Negation: `attribute_not(name, inner)` → `:not([name])`, or admit `not(..)` as a pseudo that may WRAP one further pseudo-class (`.sX:not([disabled]):hover`) — the second is the general one and needs the one-per-slot rule relaxed for `not(..)` only. Rec: (2b), fenced to `not(` heads. (3) Docs: styling.md's condition table gains the presence row and the negation row; the `child_relation` message gains a steer ('for a state on the element itself, `attribute(..)`').

**Pins.** `attribute("data-selected", None, ..)` emits `.sX[data-selected]`; `Some` unchanged (control, the existing pins); `not([disabled])` wrapping `hover` emits `.sX:not([disabled]):hover`; a second non-`not` pseudo under `not` still refused; specificity ordering against the plain `hover` rule stated and pinned (`(0,3,0)` over `(0,2,0)`).

items.title: NEW — DEAD CSS from every intermediate `Style` in a condition nest: `Style::rule` (style.vl:935, the one chokepoint) calls `emit("css", ..)` at CONSTRUCTION, so `attribute(.., hover(inner))` puts the inner `hover(..)` style's own `.sY:hover{..}` on the sheet beside the composed `.sX[..]:hover{..}` although `sY` never reaches an element — one dead rule set per nesting level per leaf declaration (`md(within(attribute(hover(x))))` emits four rule sets for one applied class); measured on a two-level probe: two of five emitted rules were for classes the bundle never applies
items.discussion: the owner's ask (2026-09-11); found while probing A89's forms (`kolt-styles-probe/forms/app.css`: `*.s1rdmbny:hover` and `*.st5yvuy:focus` emitted, neither class in app.js); pre-existing since the combinators shipped — every `hover(style().background(..))` in kolt pays it
items.body:
**Mechanism.** `Style::rule` is the only place a rule is minted and it emits on the spot; a combinator (`hover` :1339, `attribute` :1470, `within` :1380, `pseudo` :1502, `child_relation` :1432) then re-mints the inner's rules under a composed condition into a NEW class and drops the inner — but the inner's emission already happened. The sheet is therefore the union of every `Style` ever constructed at const time, not of the styles applied.

**Fix.** Emit at APPLICATION, not construction: `rule` records `(class, rendered_rule)` on the `Style` (beside `rules`), and the sheet receives a style's rendered rules when the style is APPLIED — `styled(..)`/the element-syntax class path — or, keeping the const-time model, when a `Style` value is BOUND at module level or returned from a `const` (the plateau the emission already relies on). A combinator then simply does not carry the inner's rendered rules forward. Alternative if application-time emission is too large: the combinators un-emit — impossible with a write-only `emit` channel, so no. Measure on kolt's sheet before/after (bytes; count of rules whose class is absent from the bundle — the probe's method); pin: a two-level nest emits exactly the composed rule; the standalone `hover` style still emits when it is itself applied (control); `ssr_differential` and `hmr_css_matrix` green.
